mechanisms: The connection's loop also ends independently of the two halves. Parent stop calls abort_all_streams(), which aborts each stream connection. A peer eof or error makes handle_stream_frame() set _error=true and end the loop, which then runs stop_send_loop(). The same doc paragraph even says "closing the client aborts any stream still open on it".
findings.consequence: The contract is stated wrongly ("only once", "never"). Readers may conclude shutdown cannot happen without both halves, or that close/drain is the only teardown path. The doc also contradicts itself.

evidence.detail: handle_stream_frame: if (!data) { _error = true; ... } — the loop ends on peer eof regardless of the local halves
client::abort_all_streams() aborts stream connections when the parent loop ends

findings.claim: stream_close() now waits for _outgoing_queue_ready before calling write_buf.close(), and this wait has no timeout or cancellation. If the front entry is stuck in send_entry(), for example because the peer has stopped reading, or the queue is still waiting on _negotiated, sink.close() and stop() are both delayed. A concurrent stop_send_loop() no longer waits for the queue either, because stream_close() replaced _outgoing_queue_ready with a ready future.
findings.basis: New wait added to the shutdown path; the request asks to check new waits for externally visible latency and cancellation effects.
mechanisms: std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, make_ready_future<>()) followed by then_wrapped(write_buf.close) makes the close depend on every previously queued entry finishing
findings.consequence: sink.close() can take longer when queued frames cannot be written. The front entry is only aborted through stop_send_loop() or abort(), which runs after this wait or from a separate error path. Neither the commit message nor the PR body mentions this latency or ordering change. stop_send_loop()'s when_all now covers only _sink_closed_future. Counterevidence: before the change, write_buf.close() also waited for any in-progress put(), so the extra delay is limited to entries that were queued but not yet started.

evidence.detail: auto queue_drained = std::exchange(_outgoing_queue_ready, make_ready_future<>());
stop_send_loop waits on when_all(_outgoing_queue_ready, _sink_closed_future); after stream_close the first future is an already-ready placeholder

findings.claim: stream_close() now waits for every previously accepted _outgoing_queue entry before it closes write_buf and calls stop().
